Chicken Pot Pie - Healthy, Easy to Make from Scratch

Ingredients:

Filling:

  • 1 cup chicken stock (I use Swanson’s unsalted)
  • 1 cup whole milk
  • 1/2 cup all-purpose flour
  • 2 teaspoons olive oil
  • 2 boneless chicken breasts cut into 1-inch pieces
  • 1 cup chopped onion
  • 2 carrots, sliced 1/8-inch thick
  • 2 stalks celery, sliced 1/8-inch thick
  • 1 cup frozen peas, thawed on a paper towel
  • 3/4 teaspoon salt (less if using salted stock)
  • pepper to taste

Crust:

  • 1 2/3 cups all-purpose flour
  • 1/4 teaspoon salt
  • 1/3 cup extra light olive oil
  • 1/3 cup 1% milk
  • eggwash (one egg yolk + 1 teaspoon water)

Instructions:

Filling:

  1. Preheat oven to 400° F.
  2. In a small bowl, whisk together stock, milk, and flour until smooth. Set aside.
  3. Heat the oil in your biggest pan over med-high heat. Cook and stir onion, carrot, & celery for 2 minutes.
  4. Add chicken. Cook & stir for 2 minutes.
  5. Stir in peas followed by chicken stock mixture, salt & pepper. Cook, uncovered, for 2-3 minutes until thick.
  6. Pour into a 9-inch deep dish pie pan. Set aside.

Crust:

  1. Combine flour and salt in a bowl.
  2. Add oil & milk all at once. Stir with a fork.
  3. Shape into a 5-inch disc and place between 2 sheets of floured wax paper. Roll into a 12-inch circle.
  4. Brush rim of pie pan with eggwash.
  5. Gently remove crust from wax paper by draping it over your arm and place onto pie. Trim away or flute overhanging crust, pressing down edges.
  6. Brush entire crust & edges with eggwash. With a sharp knife, poke about a dozen holes in the top to release steam.
  7. Place on a foil-lined baking sheet. Bake for 25 minutes. Let stand at least 20 minutes before serving.

Back in January my fiance and I lived in a small college town in Virginia. We lived in an apartment complex that is just far enough away from campus to not attract crazy college kids but close enough to campus to not have to deal with sketchy townies. However, this university was on winter break last week so our complex was completely dead. Maybe 4 or 5 cars in our parking lot when it generally has 25 or so. Anytime the college is on any break and students aren't around is when this complex starts to crawl with creepers though. Addicts, homeless people, thieves...you name it and this complex experienced it for the 5 years I was there.

For reference, we lived in 2 bedroom duplex. You walk in the front door and the stairs leading to the bedrooms and bathroom is directly ahead of you. To your left is 4 stairs that drop down into the living room and kitchen.

Anyway, it was about 12:45AM and my fiance and I couldn't sleep. We had just gotten a new dog earlier that evening so we were too excited to sleep. She got out her Kindle and started to read a few chapters while I went downstairs to get my laptop. About 15 minutes after getting upstairs I was perusing some paranormal websites when I heard our neighbors small two pound terror dogs start going absolutely crazy. They usually bark whenever they see anybody outside, but tonight was different. It sounded like they were trying to attack whoever was outside, while absolutely losing their minds.

Suddenly I heard a thud coming from downstairs, which didn't bother me because I thought it may have been the neighbors getting home as they were pretty noisy. Then I heard our door open. The reason I know it was our door is because we had carpet and our door makes a very distinct sound when opened, while the neighbors house had hardwood and makes no noise. Hearing this I was on alert, but still thinking(hoping) I may have heard wrong. After a minute or so I start hearing shuffling coming from downstairs and start getting a bit anxious but am trying to convince myself that it was next door.

The next thing I know I hear footsteps very slowly coming up our stairs and started to panic a little bit(all the while hoping it was the neighbors). Whatever this was got to the top step and just paused for a second before creeping up to our bedroom door. The next sound I heard sent me into battle mode as it confirmed that somebody was in our house. I heard two very light taps on our door, which got the fiances attention as well(This just confirmed that I wasn't hearing things). After hearing this I closed my laptop and started listening. Maybe 30 seconds after the taps on the door, our doorknob jiggles. Thankfully we sleep with the door locked so the intruder did not get in.

Right then was when I lept out of bed and told the fiance to call the cops while I started moving some heavy items in front of the door. When I started to do this, even though my fiance didn't hear it, I heard somebody run down our steps and out the front door.Luckily, the police got there in less than 4 minutes and cleared the house, finding nothing. Everything was locked up tight as well. My personal theory is that it was a sketchy townie person wandering around apartment complexes in the town breaking into houses to see if it was occupied or not since our town is completely dead. Our house was incredibly easy to break into as we didn't have a deadbolt on the front door, just a knob lock so I reckon the person probably jimmied it open and was creeping around. When he/they came upstairs and saw our light on from under the door I guess that he knocked to see if he would get a response or if we just left the light on while we were out and then jiggled the knob when he got no response. When he heard movement from our room I guess he hightailed it out of our house while locking everything to make it seem like nobody was there.

Ironically enough, not 24 hours prior to this happening I was musing to my fiance as we drove through town that we could probably break into almost every building in town because it was so dead. Didn't expect that to happen though!

Thankfully we have moved out of that area into a much nicer and safer area with a door that has 3 deadbolts and a chain on it, so we are at ease now. A week before we moved out back in May a crime spree hit that complex where 4 or 5 houses were broken into and completely robbed all within a 2 week time frame. They haven't caught the people yet. So glad to be out of there...it was a shithole.
